title: A repeated diagram enclosure carries cardinality only if shape-count invariance holds
summary: GDT355 observes the same broad curved-lobe idiom in an eight-compartment subseries and a nearby twelve-lobe page. A restricted structural semantic constraint is that any diagram model treating enclosure shape as a count/value operator must predict count invariance within the predeclared shape class; otherwise the shape is notation or layout rather than a numeral carrier.

design.mechanism: shape-count invariant versus shape as nonnumeric notation/layout
design.unit: predeclared diagram enclosure class with independently counted compartments and an independently observed repeated semantic label or slot
design.contrast: same enclosure geometry entails one cardinality/value class versus geometry is reusable notation whose cardinality is supplied separately
design.prediction: Within a held enclosure class, all independently segmented occurrences should have the same compartment count and preserve the same count-bearing slot relation; one verified count change falsifies the numeral-carrier rule.
design.countermodel: A diagram designer can reuse a curved-lobe template for different cardinalities, or the apparent class can collapse distinct topologies; then shape recurrence does not encode a fixed number.
design.falsifier: A source-observed repeated enclosure class contains two independently counted cardinalities, or the count varies while the proposed count-bearing slot remains unchanged.
design.principal_risk: GDT355 is an external diagram comparator and supplies no Voynich semantic label or value binding; the proposal constrains a future diagram claim rather than translating a surface.
design.related: Near GDT354/GDT355 and the closed INLINE_PROSE_FIGURE_CARDINALITY route, but it tests a conditional geometry-to-count invariant and does not infer a roster, phase order, or one-group/one-figure ownership.

source_evidence.quote:
- The exact narrow spiral-band rendering is a real local subseries: three
  adjacent pages, all with eight curved text-bearing compartments.
- The broader eight-curved-compartment family contains five pages after adding
  two decorated petal-like predecessors.
- Curved compartments are not an eight-value key. A nearby page has twelve
  curved, text-bearing lobes around a central circle.
- Four other surfaces have a clear eightfold primary division rendered as
  straight sectors or interlaced circles.

Thus the f68v3 resemblance is not an isolated doodle, but neither is it a
specific semantic match. LJS 443 demonstrates a local design vocabulary in
which eightfold systems and curved radial compartments recur, while the same
general lobe idiom also carries a different cardinality.

design.smallest_next_step: Use already admitted diagram tables to identify one repeated enclosure class with independently counted compartments; do not open images or assign meanings until the class definition and count are fixed.
